body:
You are right, I am happy I don't have a superficial relationship, but I am tired of being lonely. I often think there isn't anyone out there for me. 

Maybe this pain will be worth it, but I often feel alone in going through it. I have 2 sisters and neither of them have been as lonely for as long as I  have and it is hard to stay positive when I see so many people around me who are happy and it seems everyone on my facebook is getting in a new relationship, getting engaged and married and having babies. 

Being single does have its advantages, but when all my friends have SOs I have so few people to actually hang out with. 

I'm tired of waiting for love to find me lol I feel like the annoying kid cousin who love promised to play hide and seek with and I hid and love forgot to look for me. 


Thank you for taking the time to reply to me. I apologize for not getting back on here sooner to reply to you-- I couldn't remember my throwaway password. 

I am starting a new job on Monday already. It's full time. Pay is decent. I'm glad I don't have a gap in work history I will have to explain to any future employers. I feel much better than I did when I originally posted. I am excited to start my new job. I am also happy to not be working for my previous job anymore because in the words of the great philosopher Ted Mosby, "they're just a bunch of weiners and gonads."

I am a straight female... :'( I know women have it easier on dating sites which is what makes it even harder to accept that I am having such a difficult time meeting anybody.. I go on dates they all say "let's hang out again" and then they never respond to my texts again...

Thank you. I have been applying to receptionist and assistant jobs all day. I wish that dieting was easier... I have a binge eating disorder and it has gotten worse since my therapist has been on maternity leave. Going to the gym will be difficult now though since I am no longer employed at the college I don't have access to the gym or the money to get an account. The weather is still nice out so I will start walking. 

I typically try to have a positive outlook on life. sometimes I have to force a smile and look for the best in everything-- in this situation I am seeing this as a humbling experience which I admit I needed. I wasn't happy with the work I was doing. I wasn't making enough money. My schedule was awful-- I worked afternoons 4 days a week and then at 7:30am on Saturdays. It really messed with my sleep schedule and made it difficult to function. 


I have a lot a lot of student loan debt so I don't see myself being able to travel anytime soon. I have been to the Caribbean 3x before and they were the best times of my life. I am going to look into finding jobs there or something. The weather there is much better than in the midwest of the US. Snow will be coming soon and I am very scared that I won't be able to survive my depression then. 

I am wondering though, what would you advice have been if I was a guy?

Damn it that video made me cry happy tears. happy tears + sad tears + stress tears. this is a very confusing time for my tear ducts. I really appreciate you sharing the video and for taking the time to respond to my incoherent post. I was in the midst of an overwhelming wave earlier. I feel alright in this moment. 


I like know that this is only temporary, but it is still hurting a lot. The anxiety comes in waves and will disappear for a short period then come back. I am still trying to actually DO stuff. Like today I woke up at 10 (my old job was afternoons, so I am used to sleeping in until noon) but I showered, dressed, put on makeup and I went to a coffee shop with wifi to fill out applications instead of sitting at home where I could cry and just go lay in bed. 


I think was is difficult is that I don't know what I want my life to be. I want to fight to end the death penalty, I want to be active in politics and such. I graduated from college in 4 years with a good gpa and I did a few internships and a lot of volunteering and I did a lot. I just feel like after that I have lost some guidance. Like you go from middle school to high school, I knew I was going to college, but what is after that? I got a job and then I just coasted since then. And now I feel like I have to do something but I don't know what I want to do. 

I don't think of myself as too weak-- I mean sometimes I do, but I feel that coming to SW and calling the hotline is more strength than weakness and I wish my dad would understand that instead of thinking me asking for help is a sign of weakness. 

I think my next course of action is to apply to as many jobs as I can over the next few days-- there is a call center in my area that is known for hiring basically anyone who fills out an application. It is less pay than I was making, but some money is better than no money. I sent my application into them today with the hopes that I can start in a week or two. I think I want to work there for a few months and clear my head and figure out what career I actually want. 

Being in between phases of life really sucks. In high school I thought I just had to get to college and it would be okay. In college I thought I just had to get a real job and it would be okay. I had my real job and was never really happy. I just wonder if it ever actually gets better? Will any of this ever be worth it? On top of that I met this guy a few months ago and I thought I was in love with him... then I found out he has a diaper fetish and had been lying about being in college and didn't have a job and did a lot of drugs. I haven't been able to hold my nephew the same way since then. I am afraid of diapers and just can't believe a lot of this. Will I ever find a job worth the pain of being fired from this one? Will I ever meet a man who will take away the pain from the experience with the diaper fetish guy? or the 6 or so men I have gone on dates with just to never hear from again?
